Prevention: Remove and bury infected crop residues from the previous crop.
Farmers should select flint and tip covered varieties.
Harvest when the cobs are at physiological maturity.
Select undamaged cobs after harvesting for shelling.
Mud traditional granaries before storing grain or use clean and undamaged storage facilities.
Keep grain store and surrounding area clean and treat grain before storage.
Disinfect old bags by immersing them in hot water (50-60C) for 5 mins.
Winnow and remove damaged and infested maize before storage.
Do not mix treated and untreated maize in the storage facility.
Sun-dry shelled maize on mats, plastic sheets or tarpaulins until the required moisture content is achieved (12.5%) and place the bagged maize on pallets.
Provide adequate ventilation by opening and closing windows during hot days.
Monitoring: Monitor cobs at maturity to ensure early harvesting.
Look for small (3-4.5 mm) dark brown to black beetles roaming on grains.
Look for exit holes and dust on grains.
LGB pheromone traps in all susceptible areas to monitor populations, remember to check traps regularly and replace the lure following the instructions on the product label.
Inspect the storage facility and surrounding area on a weekly basis.
Grain treatment should be carried out when one insect is noticed and redone if one insect is seen if previously treated.
Record all treatments carried out on stack cards.
Direct Control: Use metalic or cemented silos, or clay pots for storage of grain.
Government research institutes rear and release a predatory beetle biological control agent - Teretrius nigrescens (Tn).
Contact your local office to inquire about release in your area.
